what: Lincoln National sells life insurance, annuities, group benefits and retirement plans in the United States, and manages the investments backing those long-dated promises.
customers: American households buying life cover and retirement income, and employers buying group benefits.
moat: A distribution network of advisers and employers built over a century, and a policy book that generates fees and spread income for decades once written.
risks: A 2023 reserve charge on a legacy life block destroyed a great deal of capital and the shares have not recovered
$6.3B of debt and an insurance balance sheet whose value moves with markets
Reported revenue swings violently, from $18.8B to $11.6B and back
opportunities: 2.5 times earnings, among the lowest valuations of any large American financial company
$9.5B of cash and analysts see about 17% upside, with 12 covering the stock
Group protection has turned profitable again after years of losses
watch: Capital levels at the insurance subsidiaries and group protection margins.
